q-137101.name: Question 1
q-137101.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,A=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 18 \\ 18 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
q-137101.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & 18 \\ 18 & 17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=24+17+18=59.
$$

q-137101.html:
Question 1
?

A=[104421],b=[41−1],W=[200010001]

Consider the matrices A and W, and the vector b above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem WA=Wb is given by

[a1818b][x1x2]=[c3]

what is the value of a+b+c?

a
12
b
42
c
−27
d
59
e
−19
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the normal equation corresponding to WAx=Wb, we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by (WA)T:

(WA)T⋅WAx=(WA)T⋅WbAT(WTW)Ax=AT(WTW)b

Now, since

WTW=[220001200012]=[400010001],

our normal equation can be written as follows:

[142041][400010001][104421][x1x2]=[142041][400010001][41−1][142041][404421][x1x2]=[142041][161−1][24181817][x1x2]=[183]

Therefore, we have

a+b+c=24+17+18=59.

q-158691.name: Question 2
q-158691.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 9 \\ 9 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
q-158691.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 27 \\ 16 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}77 & 9 \\ 9 & 86\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -56\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=77+86+(-56)=107.
$$

q-137921.name: Question 3
q-137921.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
q-137921.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 8 & -16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & -48 \\ -48 & 96\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -48 & -12 \\ -48 & 96 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}24 & -48 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=1.
$$

To get the normal equation corresponding to WAx=Wb, we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by (WA)T:

Now, since

q-137930.name: Question 4
q-137930.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 11 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $a+\frac{b}{c}?$
q-137930.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 11 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -4 & -12 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 44 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & 27 \\ 27 & 81\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-81 \\ -243\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 27 & -81 \\ 27 & 81 & -243\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 27 & -81 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-9-3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-9-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=-9+\frac{(-3)}{1}=-12.

Question 4
?

A=[26−1−313],b=[−22117],W=[100020001].

Consider the matrices A and W, and the vector b shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem WAx=Wb is [a0]+x2[bc],x2∈R, what is the value of a+bc?

a
15
b
6
c
−12
d
−6
e
−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the normal equation corresponding to WAx=Wb, we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by (WA)T:

(WA)T⋅WAx=(WA)T⋅WbAT(WTW)Ax=AT(WTW)b

Now, since

WTW=[120002200012]=[100040001],

our normal equation can be written as follows:

[2−116−33][100040001][26−1−313][x1x2]=[2−116−33][100040001][−22117][2−116−33][26−4−1213][x1x2]=[2−116−33][−22447][9272781][x1x2]=[−81−243]

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[927−812781−243]R2:=R2−3R1∼[927−81000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we have x1=−9−3x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[−9−3x2x2]=[−90]+x2[−31],x2∈R.

Therefore, we have

a+bc=−9+(−3)1=−12.
